question: Your Agent SDK tool generated a boilerplate data export module for a legacy billing system. Tests show three problems: the date parser returns local time instead of UTC, the file naming step builds file names from those parsed dates, and the command-line help text misspells an option name. A change to the date parser changes what the file naming step must do, but the typo affects nothing else. How should you communicate these problems to the agent?

options.text: Describe the date parsing and file naming problems together in one detailed message, then fix the help text typo in a separate iteration.
options.reason: The guide says to address interacting issues in a single detailed message and to iterate sequentially on independent issues. The date and file name problems interact, but the typo is independent.

options.text: Send all three problems in one detailed message, because every problem from a single test run should always be reported together.
options.reason: The guide ties the single-message approach to interacting issues, not to the test run that found them. The independent typo suits sequential iteration.

options.text: Combine the help text typo with the date parsing problem in one message, and report the file naming problem in a later message on its own.
options.reason: This plan groups the wrong problems. It splits the two interacting problems, which the guide says belong in one message, and bundles in the independent typo.

options.text: Report the file naming problem first, and report the date parsing problem in a later message once the file names pass the tests.
options.reason: The guide reserves sequential fixing for independent issues. Here the file naming fix depends on the date parser, so a separate fix would likely be redone after the parser changes.
